q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of this letter.)
By the oath of the pen
(that recorded the destiny of creation in the “Lowhul Mahfoodh”)
(the angels who record the actions of people)
v.s: Nūn. By the pen and what they inscribe,
v.c: Nũn. By the pen and what everyone writes!

q: By the grace of your Rabb, you
v.s: You are not, [O Muhammad], by the favor of your Lord, a madman.
v.c: By the grace of your Lord, you ˹O Prophet˺ are not insane.

q: (because of your tireless efforts to propagate Islam)
you shall have a reward that never comes to an end
(so do not grieve over the taunts of the Mushrikeen).
v.s: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
v.c: You will certainly have a never-ending reward.

v.s: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
v.c: And you are truly ˹a man˺ of outstanding character.

q: (when the Mushrikeen suffer the consequences of their Shirk)
you shall see and they will also see...
v.s: So you will see and they will see.
v.c: Soon you and the pagans will see,

q: (they will then realise that they were insane not to accept your message).
v.s: Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil].
v.c: which of you is mad.

q: Indeed only your Rabb knows best who deviates
from His path and only He knows those who are rightly guided
(and He will punish and reward people accordingly).
v.s: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
v.c: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: So do not obey those who reject
v.s: Then do not obey the deniers.
v.c: So do not give in to the deniers.
v.h: Warning the Prophet About the Deniers

q: (the beliefs of your Deen, which would then conform with their beliefs)
(by accepting only some parts of Islaam).
v.s: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
v.c: They wish you would compromise so they would yield ˹to you˺.

q: (In the following seven verses, Allaah refers specifically to Waleed bin Mughiera, who was one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's worst enemies. However, his description fits many Kuffaar.)
(on every occasion, whether a matter be true or false),
v.s: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
v.c: And do not obey the despicable, vain oath-taker,

q: ...who searches for the faults of others, who excels in carrying tales
v.s: [And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -
v.c: slanderer, gossip-monger,

v.s: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,
v.c: withholder of good, transgressor, evildoer,

q: harsh and whose parentage is uncertain as well.
v.s: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.
v.c: brute, and—on top of all that—an illegitimate child.

q: because he has wealth and sons
(and therefore very proudly feels that he can do as he pleases).
v.s: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,
v.c: Now, ˹simply˺ because he has been blessed with ˹abundant˺ wealth and children,

q: When Our Aayaat are recited to him, he says, “These are fables
v.s: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
v.c: whenever Our revelations are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”

q: We shall soon brand him on his snout
(on his nose in the Aakhirah because of his arrogance).
v.s: We will brand him upon the snout.
v.c: We will soon mark his snout.

q: (the Mushrikeen of Makkah whose wealth and children caused them to become arrogant)
as We tested the people of the orchard
(a few brothers who owned an orchard)
when they swore that they will pluck the fruit
(so that they would not have to give any of the produce to the poor who usually gathered therefor a share)...
v.s: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning
v.c: Indeed, We have tested those ˹Meccans˺ as We tested the owners of the garden—when they swore they would surely harvest ˹all˺ its fruit in the early morning,
v.h: The Test of the Garden Owners

v.s: Without making exception.
v.c: leaving no thought for Allah’s Will.

q: from your Rabb swept over their orchard as they slept.
v.s: So there came upon it [i.e., the garden] an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
v.c: Then it was struck by a torment from your Lord while they slept,

q: So their orchard had become like a harvested crop by the morning
(completely bare, without any trace of the produce whatsoever leftover).
v.s: And it became as though reaped.
v.c: so it was reduced to ashes.

q: (Unaware of what had happened the previous night,)
called to each other in the morning...
v.s: And they called one another at morning,
v.c: Then by daybreak they called out to each other,

q: “Leave early for the plantation if you wish to pluck the harvest.”
v.s: [Saying], "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit."
v.c: ˹saying,˺ “Go early to your harvest, if you want to pick ˹all˺ the fruit.”

q: they whispered to each other saying...
v.s: So they set out, while lowering their voices,
v.c: So they went off, whispering to one another,

q: ...“No needy person should ever enter your presence today.”
v.s: [Saying], "There will surely not enter it today upon you [any] poor person."
v.c: “Do not let any poor person enter your garden today.”

q: They proceeded with the thought that they had the power to withhold
v.s: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.
v.c: And they proceeded early, totally fixated on their purpose.

q: they exclaimed, “We must have lost the way!
v.s: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;
v.c: But when they saw it ˹devastated˺, they cried, “We must have lost ˹our˺ way!

q: (When they realised that the orchard was indeed theirs, they said,)
v.s: Rather, we have been deprived."
v.c: In fact, we have been deprived ˹of our livelihood˺.”

q: The good one among them said, “Did I not tell you
(not to stop giving charity to the poor).
v.s: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [God]?'"
v.c: The most sensible of them said, “Did I not urge you to say, ‘Allah willing.’?”

v.s: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
v.c: They replied, “Glory be to our Lord! We have truly been wrongdoers.”

q: (Thereafter, like most people do during times of distress,)
They turned to each other pinning the blame on one another.
v.s: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.
v.c: Then they turned on each other, throwing blame.

q: (When they finally realised that they were all to be blamed,)
They cried, “Woe be to us! We have
v.s: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors.
v.c: They said, “Woe to us! We have certainly been transgressors.

q: “We hope that our Rabb will replace for us something better than our orchard
(either in this world or in the Aakhirah).
Indeed we have confidence in our Rabb
v.s: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."
v.c: We trust our Lord will give us a better garden than this, ˹for˺ we are indeed turning to our Lord with hope.”

q: (of Allaah in this world for the sinners).
However, the punishment of the Aakhirah is much more severe. If only they
v.s: Such is the punishment [of this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
v.c: That is the ˹way of Our˺ punishment ˹in this world˺. But the punishment of the Hereafter is certainly far worse, if only they knew.

q: Verily those with Taqwa shall have Jannaat of bliss close to their Rabb
v.s: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure.
v.c: Indeed, the righteous will have the Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.

q: Should We treat the obedient ones in the same manner as
v.s: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
v.c: Should We then treat those who have submitted like the wicked?

q: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
(How can the Kuffaar and sinners ever think that they will receive rewards equal to what the people of Taqwa receive?)
v.s: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
v.c: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?

q: (you say that all will be treated equally because)
book with you that you study...
v.s: Or do you have a scripture in which you learn
v.c: Or do you have a scripture, in which you read

q: ...in which there are things mentioned that appeal to you
(such as the promise that you will enter Jannah regardless of what you do in the world)?
v.s: That indeed for you is whatever you choose?
v.c: that you will have whatever you choose?

q: you have an oath from Us that will last until Qiyaamah stating that you shall have whatever
v.s: Or do you have oaths [binding] upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?
v.c: Or do you have oaths binding on Us until the Day of Judgment that you will have whatever you decide?

q: which of them will stand guarantee for this.
v.s: Ask them which of them, for that [claim], is responsible.
v.c: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ which of them can guarantee all that.

q: (that they ascribe to Allaah who will stand guarantee for this)?
Let them bring their partners if they are truthful.
v.s: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.
v.c: Or do they have associate-gods ˹supporting this claim˺? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods, if what they say is true.

q: (it will be so magnificent that by seeing it)
to prostrate but will be unable to
(because only the true Mu'mineen will be able to prostrate in obedience).
v.s: The Day the shin will be uncovered and they are invited to prostration but they [i.e., the disbelievers] will not be able,
v.c: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Shin ˹of Allah˺ will be bared, and the wicked will be asked to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so,

q: Their gazes will be cast down
and disgrace shall overcome them. Indeed they used to be summoned to prostrate
when they were hail and healthy
(but they refused to do so. Therefore, in the Aakhirah they will be unable to do so also).
v.s: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.
v.c: with eyes downcast, totally covered with disgrace. For they were ˹always˺ called to prostrate ˹in the world˺ when they were fully capable ˹but they chose not to˺.

q: with the one who rejects this speech
We shall gradually lead them on
(allow them to continue sinning without punishing them)
in a manner that they do not realise.
(Thinking that punishment will not arrive, the Kuffaar continue sinning, not realising that they are earning for themselves a terrible punishment.)
v.s: So leave Me, [O Muhammad], with [the matter of] whoever denies this statement [i.e., the Qur’ān]. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.
v.c: So leave to Me ˹O Prophet˺ those who reject this message. We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend.

q: (temporary relief by not punishing them immediately).
(they will be unable to escape My plan).
v.s: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
v.c: I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless.

q: (the Kuffaar rejecting your message, O Rasulullaah ﷺ? because they think that)
and they feel burdened by a penalty
(and therefore prefer not to listen to your preaching)?
v.s: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down?
v.c: Or are you asking them for a reward ˹for the message˺ so that they are overburdened by debt?

q: (reject the message of Islaam because they firmly believe that they)
(which advises them not to accept the guidance of Rasulullaah ﷺ and),
v.s: Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
v.c: Or do they have access to ˹the Record in˺ the unseen, so they copy it ˹for all to see˺?

q: be patient with the decision of your Rabb
(hasty for the punishment to come to them immediately)
like the person of the fish
(while in the stomach of the fish).
v.s: Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muhammad], and be not like the companion of the fish [i.e., Jonah] when he called out while he was distressed.
v.c: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not be like ˹Jonah,˺ the Man of the Whale, who cried out ˹to Allah˺, in total distress.

m: surely he would have been thrown
q: If the grace of his Rabb did not reach him, he would have been cast on to the bare shore
(without assistance because he left his town prior to Allaah's permission). (However, Allaah shaded him on the shore and provided food for him there.)
v.s: If not that a favor [i.e., mercy] from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.
v.c: Had he not been shown grace by his Lord, he would have certainly been cast onto the open ˹shore˺, still blameworthy.

q: His Rabb selected him and made him among the righteous.
v.s: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
v.c: Then his Lord chose him, making him one of the righteous.

q: When the Kuffaar hear the Reminder
it seems as if they could almost make you
and they say, “He is certainly insane!”
v.s: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes [i.e., looks] when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."
v.c: The disbelievers would almost cut you down with their eyes when they hear ˹you recite˺ the Reminder, and say, “He is certainly a madman.”

q: is but a Reminder for the universe.
v.s: But it is not except a reminder to the worlds.
v.c: But it is simply a reminder to the whole world.
